data.body:
Implemented and pushed as Gerrit change 2548 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2548), from an isolated worktree off origin/main so it does not stack on the currently-red six-change stack.

AC1: test_relation_vocabulary_is_pinned_three_ways feeds the three REAL sides (CANONICAL_RELATIONS, get_args(types.Relation), the common.schema.json relation enum) to a pure _relation_parity_failure helper. No relation is re-listed anywhere in the test.

AC2: four divergence tests, each perturbing one side of an agreeing baseline and asserting the message names that side and the offending relation, plus the additive case where the two sides LACKING the new relation are both named. Anti-tautology proven separately by mutating each REAL source in turn: dropping caused_by from CANONICAL_RELATIONS, supersedes from the schema enum, duplicates from the Literal. The parity test went RED each time, naming that side.

AC3: the docs arm is byte-identical. 426 tests in tests/interfaces/contracts pass; lint and typecheck clean.

Two process notes worth keeping. (1) My first schema mutation was a silent no-op: I built the replacement string from json.dumps formatting while the real enum is a single line, so the suite stayed green and I would have recorded that as evidence. Re-ran with a verified git diff before each mutation run. (2) The divergence tests first derived their perturbed inputs from the live sides, so one real drift cascaded five failures over a single root cause. They now perturb a self-consistent baseline read from the schema, so a real drift fails only the parity test, plus the docs arm as a genuine second signal.
